page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c16g1.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by KVM virtualization. The instance features an x86_64 architecture driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores via hyperthreading. Cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 33 MB shared L3 cache, with instruction support covering AVX, AVX-512F, FMA, and AES. Memory provision stands at 62.0 GB RAM, giving approximately 3.88 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single dedicated NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB VRAM. There is no bundled local storage, requiring external network-attached storage, while the baseline network throughput is rated at 6 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes show clear divergence between general-purpose host CPU processing and GPU acceleration. CPU-bound metrics demonstrate modest capability: Geekbench single-core sits at 937.0 and stress-ng single-core reports 1110.08, both ranking in the lower quartile. Single-threaded gzip compression at 19.33 GB/sec also shows restricted per-core processing rates. Multi-core operations scale reliably, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core rating of 5951.0, PassMark CPU aggregate score of 13056.17, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 57.55 GB/sec, placing overall CPU compute density in the mid-tier. Cached memory read throughput reaches 659.86 GB/sec, tapering to 73.63 GB/sec on uncached large blocks and 53.83 GB/sec on sequential writes.

Conversely, hardware-assisted deep learning benchmarks perform at top-tier levels. The NVIDIA T4 enables LLM prompt processing speeds of 8410.67 tokens per second on lightweight 135M parameter models and 1141.42 tokens per second on 7B parameter models. Text generation throughput reaches 248.25 tokens per second for 135M architectures and 34.57 tokens per second for 7B models. These metrics showcase efficient tensor processing capabilities for inference pipelines, compensating for lower baseline host CPU speeds.

The ecs.gn6i-c16g1.4xlarge presents an economical resource trade-off for teams seeking specialized GPU inference and computer vision capabilities without paying for high-end server-class host processors. While unsuitable for heavy single-thread processing or local storage-intensive caching tasks, it fits batch inference, deep learning model deployment up to 7B parameters, GPU-accelerated video transcoding, image processing pipelines, and mid-tier AI microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c16g1.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) on a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor, 62.0 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU offering 16 GB VRAM. It operates on KVM virtualization without bundled local storage and includes a 6 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark profiles highlight weaker single-core compute performance alongside mid-range multi-core scaling. However, the integrated NVIDIA T4 accelerator provides exceptional efficiency for machine learning inference, delivering prompt processing speeds up to 8410.67 tokens per second on small models and 1141.42 tokens per second on 7B architectures. Given its memory-to-vCPU allocation and GPU pairing, the instance is well matched for mid-sized deep learning inference, image processing pipelines, video transcoding, and GPU-driven web serving workloads.
